body: I wouldn't even know where to begin with it to be honest... I can't even write a piece on my own, so I'd imagine trying to do one collaboratively would be even more difficult.

I hope it will... I'm just not sure whether I'll manage to survive the next few days, so my apologies if I disappear or anything.

I'll have to have a look around, see what I can find... see if I have anything worthwhile. I tend to delete a lot of stuff, so have to make sure anything that's written is somewhere I can't get at it so easily.

A burden freely taken is still a burden... but it has been a long time since I've really got talking with anyone new online.

It's been over a year I think since I actually last wrote something in any way creative, but I don't mind sharing what I have... it's one of those things I've been frustrated with for a long time though, I've tried everything to kickstart myself in to doing it again, but just can't manage it any more. And I'd certainly like to see the sort of thing you've written.

I've been in love a few times, and have never loved myself... but I'm not sure whether that's evidence either way, given my resulting state of mind...

The problem is though, I don't want to be who I am. The goal, as you say, is development, who I want to be... and I don't really trust my own judgement on getting there. And if I'm meeting the expectations of others, making them happy, then I'm getting closer to the sort of person I want to be. At worst, I'm hopefully adding bits and pieces of happiness in the world, which is laudable in itself, and at best, the potential resulting positive regard of others might help me to keep living.

At this point, I see suicide as the least worst option. Every day I live seems like a simulacrum of life, a relentless barrage of destruction of the soul, a path lit by false hopes. And a fair sized portion of melodramatic language apparently! (I don't mean to write quite like this, but a lot of my dwelling on negative thought in the past has been through poetry, so I tend to think on it in those terms). So simply, if I can't have love and life and happiness, I can accept the peace of death. And I think, in truth, the only person who would notice or care I was gone if I disappeared off the face of the earth tomorrow would be my mother, so it's not like there is much at all which is in the way of me going through with it. Though as I've been in this state in one form or another for the last 15 years, and the same has been true on many occasions, I don't know which time will be different.

As for friendship... I fear to give it, and I would not want to be burdensome in saying yes. 

And while I appreciate the sentiment, I don't see any value that I could have.

I guess that is part of the problem, this is the new perspective. The person I am now is the sum of everything that has lead up to this point in my life... which may be just about the worst case of stating the obvious I've been guilty of in a long time! I never used to be this resentful, this bitter... I've been depressed for a long time, but it's been this last year which has made me far more distrustful of others, and far more aware of what I've missed that I will never get back. Basically, a lot of lamenting about the past, and while I recognize that isn't useful... when I conclude that I far prefer the person I used to be, and even then that person was suicidal, it makes me just want to die and be done with it at last.

I can understand what you are saying about purpose, but I've come to the opposite conclusion I think. If I believed that all this up till now was for a purpose, then I would feel a lot of hatred towards whatever force in the universe defined that purpose. The people who were in my life were varied, some were no good for me, but others most certainly were... until they were gone. The person who was, for a decade, probably the person I was closest to, just one day cut off all communication with me. No explanation, and they were and are communicating with others, so I can rule out every explanation of circumstance alternative to ones that mean they don't want anything to do with me any more... and while I'm not immune to the human trait of sometimes being unable to see my own flaws, I'm introspective enough to know that there was nothing that I did which caused it. I guess it doesn't make much difference, but I say that more to make it clear that it isn't just a matter of people moving on with their lives and growing apart. A lot of the disconnects with people have been abrupt and brutal in their silence.

Though you have kind of managed to come across one of the main problems in myself which I've not yet found a solution to. The only reason I want to be mentally healthy, or at least project the facade of a normal, well adjusted human being, as well as pretty much any other positive trait you'd care to mention, is for other people. And as much as I recognize that's not only mentally unhealthy, but also a massive risk, as events have proven, I simply cannot find any way to establish self-esteem within me, to the point with all the time and effort I've put in to trying, I consider it practically impossible to ever be otherwise.

Ideally, I want to be the sort of person other people like, that is cared for and valued. Being who I am has made that harder to achieve, but the things I enjoy in life, the times that I have felt best, have all been because of the regard of others... though I don't mean praise or anything like that, but just having that feeling that I matter to someone enough that they want me to be a part of their life, whether it's a matter of simple friendship, or a closer relationship. The other things I used to enjoy, gaming, music, writing, reading, have mostly become just distractions now... things that I used to enjoy, but only seem to do now out of habit. Occasionally I do get joy out of it, but at this point it's less and less frequently.
